claim: Imports a local track, marks a cue, exports a cue file, and restores the saved cue after reload.
sandbox: fresh browser context with generated WAV; reload as soon as the cue appears, then assert the cue and note survive before exporting

claim: A saved set and the sample demo work offline after the first visit.
sandbox: two dedicated browser contexts; save generated WAV and prime sample demo, wait for service worker, go offline, reload, and assert both workspaces

claim: Tracks stay in the browser and are not uploaded.
sandbox: fresh demo context records all requests during sample playback, editing, export, reset, and exit

claim: Cue-file exports do not include audio bytes.
sandbox: sample demo; parse downloaded JSON and assert audio metadata only

claim: Cuebook keeps more than five cues and imports the full cue sheet.
sandbox: fresh browser with six-cue fixture; import, reload, and assert all six cues remain

claim: Cuebook saves a WebM rehearsal when track-audio capture is supported; otherwise it explains how to recover.
sandbox: fresh browser with generated WAV and no purchase state; assert a WebM download, then remove canvas capture and assert recovery guidance

claim: Every user can select Contour, Orbit, and Shards scenes.
sandbox: sample demo; select each named scene and assert pressed state

claim: A scene renders the same frame whenever the playhead returns to the same track time.
sandbox: sample demo; hash canvas pixels at one timeline position, move away and return

claim: Cuebook includes an installable standalone app shell.
sandbox: fresh browser; assert manifest, icons, and activated service worker

claim: The one-click demo starts with five audible sample cues and never changes real project storage.
sandbox: seed a real IndexedDB project; exercise demo edit, reset, reload, and exit; assert the real project is unchanged

claim: Cuebook has no analytics, trackers, third-party runtime scripts, or CDN font requests.
sandbox: record requests through home and demo flows and inspect built HTML/CSS/JS origins

claim: All current Cuebook rehearsal tools are available without a purchase.
sandbox: fresh browser; assert free copy, no checkout or billing links, no purchase copy, and no billing requests

claim: Beat numbers use the BPM and offset entered, while cue time stays at the selected track time.
sandbox: sample demo; change BPM and offset, then assert a selected cue's displayed beat changes while its time remains selected

claim: Keyboard controls and screen-reader labels are available without a purchase.
sandbox: fresh browser with generated WAV; use keyboard Mark cue and assert labelled controls expose accessible names

claim: Cuebook builds as a static app with no required environment variable or backend.
sandbox: serve fresh dist build; run core demo and scan built files for required runtime environment placeholders
